heading: Vision → Loop → Evidence
introduction: Your product evolves through priorities, decisions, and discoveries. LangDrift connects the direction you intended with the changes made along the way and the evidence that explains them. Explore how those changes can reveal a gap, a deliberate trade-off, or a better direction.
driftExplanation: Drift can reveal a gap, a course correction, or a valuable discovery. Its meaning comes from context and evidence.

priority-shift.context: A customer request moves advanced configuration earlier in onboarding. The team needs to understand how that priority affects the original first-use experience.

vision.target: Help a new workspace owner reach a useful first result before asking them to configure advanced settings.
vision.audience: Small teams setting up their first workspace without dedicated technical support.
vision.successCriterion: A new owner can complete the core workflow with sensible defaults and adjust advanced settings afterward.

request.label: Request
request.description: A prospective customer asks for advanced configuration before their evaluation can begin.

change.label: Change
change.description: The team brings the configuration step forward in the onboarding flow.

review.label: Review
review.description: The request explains the new priority, but the records do not establish whether the trade-off for first-time users was accepted.

priority-target.title: Onboarding target
priority-target.summary: The original brief puts the first useful result before advanced configuration.
priority-target.sourceContext: The brief describes workspace owners who need to try the core workflow without technical help. It treats advanced settings as a later step, after the owner has seen an initial result.

priority-request.title: Evaluation requirement
priority-request.summary: The customer request explains why configuration became a near-term priority.
priority-request.sourceContext: The request says configuration is necessary for this customer's evaluation. It does not establish that the same requirement should apply to every new workspace owner.

priority-flow.title: Revised onboarding flow
priority-flow.summary: The revised flow places configuration before the first result, creating tension with the original criterion.
priority-flow.sourceContext: The review describes the new step order. These records do not include a decision explicitly accepting the effect on the broader onboarding audience, so that intent still needs to be checked.

interpretation.title: A priority shift to review
interpretation.description: The product now asks for configuration earlier than the original target intended. The customer request explains the pressure behind that change, but it does not explain whether the broader onboarding trade-off was accepted. That distinction gives the team a concrete decision to revisit.
interpretation.openQuestion: Should this requirement apply only to the customer's evaluation, or should the team intentionally revise the onboarding target?

product-trade-off.context: The team accepts a temporary manual setup step to deliver a requested integration sooner, and records when that compromise should be reviewed.

vision.target: Help a new workspace owner reach a useful first result with a guided setup and minimal manual work.
vision.audience: Small teams connecting their first data source without a dedicated integration specialist.
vision.successCriterion: The owner can connect the data needed for the core workflow through the guided setup, without copying configuration values manually.

decision.label: Decision
decision.description: The team accepts manual configuration for the first release of a requested integration.

delivery.label: Delivery
delivery.description: The integration becomes available sooner, while its setup still requires additional effort.

review-condition.label: Review condition
review-condition.description: Revisit the compromise before broad rollout, using support feedback and setup observations.

tradeoff-target.title: Guided setup target
tradeoff-target.summary: The target calls for a guided connection flow without manual configuration copying.
tradeoff-target.sourceContext: The brief prioritizes owners who do not have a dedicated integration specialist. Its setup criterion is about reducing manual work, rather than simply making an integration available.

tradeoff-decision.title: Temporary setup compromise
tradeoff-decision.summary: The decision explicitly accepts manual setup for the initial release to bring the integration forward.
tradeoff-decision.sourceContext: The team records the expected extra setup effort and the reason for accepting it. The decision also calls for a review before broad rollout; it does not claim that the extra effort is harmless.

tradeoff-release.title: Integration release scope
tradeoff-release.summary: The release review confirms that the integration is available with the documented manual step.
tradeoff-release.sourceContext: The review matches the delivered flow to the accepted scope. Support feedback and setup observations are still needed to decide whether the compromise remains appropriate for a wider audience.

interpretation.title: A deliberate trade-off
interpretation.description: The team accepted additional setup effort to deliver the integration sooner. The decision records why the compromise was made and when it should be revisited. Understanding that context helps leadership decide whether the trade-off still serves the product vision.
interpretation.openQuestion: What would need to be true before this manual setup is acceptable for a broader rollout?

new-opportunity.context: Interviews and a small prototype exercise suggest that explaining setup choices may matter more than removing another step.

vision.target: Help a new workspace owner reach a useful first result through a short, straightforward onboarding flow.
vision.audience: New owners who understand their work but are unfamiliar with the product's setup choices.
vision.successCriterion: The owner can complete a short flow and understand the choices needed to produce a useful result.

discovery.label: Discovery
discovery.description: Interviews surface uncertainty about what the setup choices mean.

experiment.label: Experiment
experiment.description: The team explores contextual guidance instead of only removing steps.

proposed-direction.label: Proposed direction
proposed-direction.description: Consider making confidence and understanding more explicit in the target, then validate the proposal with a broader sample.

opportunity-interviews.title: Setup interviews
opportunity-interviews.summary: Interview participants describe uncertainty about the choices, not only the length of the flow.
opportunity-interviews.sourceContext: The notes record questions about which setup option fits a participant's intended workflow. They suggest a possible explanation for hesitation, without establishing how common that explanation is across all users.

opportunity-prototype.title: Contextual guidance exercise
opportunity-prototype.summary: In the small prototype exercise, participants use the explanations to describe their next choice more clearly.
opportunity-prototype.sourceContext: The exercise adds short explanations beside the setup choices. The observations support further investigation, but they do not establish a production conversion improvement or a broadly validated outcome.

opportunity-proposal.title: Proposed target refinement
opportunity-proposal.summary: A draft proposes emphasizing confident decisions alongside a short onboarding flow.
opportunity-proposal.sourceContext: The proposal would make understanding the setup choices a more explicit success criterion. It remains a proposal until reviewed; the current Vision Target has not been automatically replaced.

interpretation.title: A discovery worth validating
interpretation.description: The evidence suggests that a better first-use experience may come from clearer guidance, rather than fewer steps alone. This could improve the product's direction. The next decision is whether the discovery is strong enough to refine the target and what further validation is needed.
interpretation.openQuestion: What additional evidence would justify changing the Vision Target for the broader onboarding audience?
